Title: Sleep Paralysis Isn't a Sign Something's Wrong - What Actually Triggers It

Description:
If you've ever woken up unable to move and thought something was wrong with you, you're not alone - and English doesn't even have an everyday word for it. An irregular sleep schedule, sleeping flat on your back, and anxiety or other mental health conditions all make sleep paralysis more likely. A steadier schedule, side sleeping, and managing stress before bed help. If episodes are frequent, mention it to a doctor - it can sometimes point to narcolepsy.
